# Consistent Meditation

On-screen:
A 20-minute practice on steadiness
Script:
Welcome. In the next twenty minutes we are going to practise one skill: coming back.

The instruction is small on purpose. If you can do the small thing, the large thing takes care of itself.

## Why consistency beats intensity

On-screen:
Short daily sits beat heroic weekends
Streak, not session length, is what changes you
Script:
Most people quit meditation because the first version they try is too big.

Twenty minutes every day for a year is 121 hours. A two-hour retreat once a month is 24. The arithmetic is not close.

Consistency wins because the skill is familiarity, and familiarity only comes from repetition.

### The five-minute floor

On-screen:
Five minutes counts
Five minutes today beats twenty tomorrow
Script:
The floor is five minutes. On a hard day you still sit for five.

Five minutes is short enough that there is no good excuse, and long enough that the mind notices the shape of the practice.

#### What a five-minute sit looks like

On-screen:
Timer on, breathe, done
Script:
Sit down, set a timer for five minutes, and follow the breath.

When the timer rings, you are done. That is the whole protocol.

## The posture that does not collapse

On-screen:
Feet grounded, spine tall, shoulders soft
Script:
Posture is not discipline. It is a way to stay awake without effort.

Feet flat on the floor. Spine tall but not stiff. Shoulders dropped until they forgive you.

Hands can rest on the knees or in the lap. Choose one and keep it.

### When the mind wanders

On-screen:
Notice, name it, return
Script:
Wandering is not failure. Noticing it is the practice.

Name it quietly: planning, worry, replaying. Then return to the next breath.

You will do this dozens of times in one sit. That is not a problem to solve. That is the exercise.

### When you feel restless

Script:
Restlessness is usually a body that has not moved today.

Before you sit, walk for two minutes. Then sit.

If it persists, shorten the sit. A short sit you finish is worth more than a long sit you abandon.

## Closing

On-screen:
Sit tomorrow
Script:
Tomorrow, sit for five minutes before you open your laptop.

That is the whole assignment. We will meet again next week.

## The month ahead

Script:
The rest of this course is four weeks long.

Each week adds one thing and takes nothing away.

### What to expect each week

On-screen:
Week one: showing up
Week two: noticing
Week three: settling
Week four: steadiness
Script:
Each week will feel different, and none of the differences mean you are doing it wrong.

### Week one

On-screen:
The mind is louder than expected
Script:
Week one usually surprises people with how loud the mind is.

This is not a side effect of meditation. It is what was always happening. You are simply still enough to hear it.

### Week two

On-screen:
Small gaps of calm
Script:
By week two you may notice small gaps between thoughts.

Do not chase them. Notice, and return.

#### Week two, in detail

On-screen:
Gaps appear without effort
Script:
The gaps are short at first. A breath, maybe two.

They lengthen on their own. You cannot lengthen them by wanting to.

##### A note on tracking

On-screen:
One mark per day, nothing more
Script:
A single mark on a calendar is enough tracking for the first month.

Detailed metrics come later, once the habit exists.
